## Overview

The Bedick, also called Bedik, are a minority ethnic group of Africa. They live in villages in the most isolated area of eastern Senegal, in the Arrondissement of Bandafassi; Iwol is one of their settlements. They speak the Bedik language. Their religion combines animist roots with more recent Christian influence. Their connections with Guinea Conakry and Mali are described as stronger than those with Senegal, and they have contact with Bassari and Serer groups. Their ancestors are identified as the families Keita and Camera, who came from Mali because of the war led by Alpha Yaye, coming from Fouta Djalon.

commons_photos.title: Femme Bédik portant son enfant attaché dans son dos.jpg
commons_photos.description:
The village of Iwol, where this photo was taken, sits on top of a hill. The women are responsible for fetching all the water needed by the village, every day, at the foot of the hill and carrying it in a container (~15lt) placed on their heads. They are also the ones who pound the millet. This explains their physical constitution which is simply magnificent and admirable.
The Bédik are a West African population living mainly in the south-east of Senegal, in the district of Bandafassi, near the border with Guinea. They constitute one of the smallest minorities (around 1% of the population). Unlike most of Senegal, the Bédik country is located at altitude.
